clue.text: Royal crime writer?

definitions.meaning: a reigning monarch's consort or a female sovereign
Ellery ... was the pen name of two American cousins who wrote detective novels

explanation.definitionFit: A female monarch is a royal personage, and Ellery Queen was a famous pseudonymous detective-story author.

clue.text: Trollope character sounds like Fletcher's creation

indicators.note: the clue says the name is heard as a phrase describing a fletcher's output

parts.note: a fletcher makes arrows, and a quiver full of them is his finished work

explanation.surface: A literary pairing: a Trollope figure whose name echoes something from another writer named Fletcher.
explanation.walkthrough: Fletcher looks like the dramatist John Fletcher; it is a fletcher, an arrow-maker. Mr Quiverful is the poor clergyman with many children in Trollope's Barchester Towers.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Quiverful is the impoverished, large-familied clergyman in Trollope's Barchester novels.

clue.text: Praise some Tales of Wessex, told by Hardy

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the words are taken, a run lying across them

explanation.surface: Hardy recounts stories set in his fictional Wessex.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles Wessex and told. Wessex is the name Thomas Hardy gave to the south-west English counties where his novels are set.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud something is to speak highly of it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Nobody could identify the captain of this submarine

definitions.text: Nobody could identify the captain of this submarine

parts.words: Nobody could identify the captain of this submarine
parts.note: the captain is Jules Verne's Nemo, Latin for 'no one', so Nobody names him; the vessel is his

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Nobody' as a name: Captain Nemo's name means 'no one' in Latin. He commands the submarine in Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Verne's Captain Nemo commands the submarine of that name in Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.

clue.text: Some stand-up characters of Greene

definitions.meaning: Graham Greene's 1966 novel set in Haiti is named after its cast of figures

explanation.definitionFit: Stand-up performers are funny people on stage, and Graham Greene's Haiti novel takes this plural as its title.

clue.text: Start of century to fuel up inspiration for historians

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word century is wanted
in a down clue the word for fuel is written upwards, so read backwards

explanation.surface: Beginning a new hundred years by refuelling gives scholars of the past their inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the start of 'century'; 'up' turns OIL into LIO. The nine Muses inspired the arts; one presides over history.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Muse of history in Greek mythology, the goddess said to inspire chroniclers.

clue.text: Her boss stood by his bond, they say

definitions.text: Her boss stood by his bond, they say

parts.words: Her boss stood by his bond, they say
parts.note: the boss is M, who stood by his agent James Bond; 'his word is his bond' is the saying behind the wording

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' reads as a promise ('my word is my bond'); it is the spy James Bond, whose chief is M, served by his secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Moneypenny is secretary to M, head of the secret service in Ian Fleming's spy stories.

clue.text: He revealed anew world in music

definitions.text: He revealed anew world in music

parts.words: He revealed anew world in music
parts.note: points to the Czech composer of the Symphony From the New World

explanation.walkthrough: 'Anew world' hides the title of the Ninth Symphony, From the New World, by the Czech composer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Czech composer wrote the Symphony No. 9, From the New World, after living in America.

clue.text: Some thoughts on Destiny by Isak Dinesen which should not have been published?

definitions.text: Some thoughts on Destiny by Isak Dinesen
definitions.meaning: ... of Destiny is a 1958 story collection by the Danish writer Isak Dinesen

definitions.text: which should not have been published?
definitions.meaning: the Greek root anekdota means things unpublished

explanation.definitionFit: Dinesen's collection bears this title, and the word comes from Greek anekdota, meaning unpublished items.

clue.text: Beautiful French outlaw immortalized by the Steinbeckian Woody Guthrie

definitions.text: Beautiful French outlaw immortalized by the Steinbeckian Woody Guthrie

parts.words: Beautiful French outlaw immortalized by the Steinbeckian Woody Guthrie
parts.note: Beautiful French is belle, so the outlaw is Belle, the American bandit queen about whom Guthrie sang

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beautiful French' gives Belle; Belle Starr was a Wild West outlaw, subject of a Woody Guthrie song. Guthrie is Steinbeckian for his Dust Bowl ballads.
explanation.definitionFit: Belle Starr was a notorious nineteenth-century American outlaw woman celebrated in folk song.

clue.text: A. E. Housman deplored that of a "comma on p.4"

definitions.text: A. E. Housman deplored that of a "comma on p.4"

parts.words: A. E. Housman deplored that of a "comma on p.4"
parts.note: Housman, a fussy proofreader, complained of an unwanted comma pushing its way into his text

explanation.walkthrough: Housman, poet and exacting classical scholar, objected to printers adding an unwanted comma to his proofs.
explanation.definitionFit: An unwanted comma forced into a text is an unwelcome entry, an imposition where it does not belong.

clue.text: Last letter of Homer? of

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Last letter of Homer? of (5)': the trailing 'of' is garbled OCR, and no scan or search gives the full printed text.

clue.text: A relic, possibly, of a delicacy more memorable than Proust's madeleine

definitions.text: a delicacy more memorable than Proust's madeleine

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the two words may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Some treasured relic of a cake, perhaps outdoing the famous madeleine that sparked Proust's memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of A RELIC. Proust's madeleine dipped in tea brings back his childhood in In Search of Lost Time.
explanation.definitionFit: This choux pastry filled with cream and topped with icing is a sweet treat, a pastry delicacy.

clue.text: Hero of early Sanders of the River story

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the words that follow, a run inside them

explanation.surface: The protagonist of an early tale from Edgar Wallace's Sanders of the River series.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'early Sanders'. Sanders of the River is Edgar Wallace's African adventure series; the answer is the Spartan commander, or the lover in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spartan admiral who defeated Athens was a celebrated war leader, and Shakespeare's young Athenian lover is a play's romantic lead.

clue.text: Hamlet's father made one

parts.note: the murdered king returns as a ghost, so 'made one' means appeared as a spectre

explanation.walkthrough: The ghost of Hamlet's murdered father walks the battlements of Elsinore.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostly appearance is a spectral sight, which is exactly what the dead king presents.

clue.text: Title by and of Ted Hughes

definitions.text: Title by and of Ted Hughes

parts.words: Title by and of Ted Hughes
parts.note: Hughes wrote a poem of this name in The Hawk in the Rain, and the phrase also describes Hughes himself

explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous Poet' is a poem in Hughes's first collection, and it also describes the Poet Laureate himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Hughes, Poet Laureate, was a celebrated versifier, and he gave one early poem this very name.

clue.text: "… of music they were the ____s, the opponents particularly of Wagner and Liszt" (Alfred Einstein)

definitions.text: "… of music they were the ____s, the opponents particularly of Wagner and Liszt" (Alfred Einstein)

parts.words: "… of music they were the ____s, the opponents particularly of Wagner and Liszt" (Alfred Einstein)
parts.note: the blank is the name for devotees of the composer of The Magic Flute, as opposed to the New German School

explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Einstein, the musicologist and not the physicist, wrote a famous study of the composer; conservatives who opposed Wagner and Liszt looked back to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirers of the Salzburg composer's classical ideals are named after him with this adjectival form.

clue.text: Attempt to start some truly awful book

indicators.note: the start of each following word gives one letter, the initials in order

explanation.surface: Trying to begin a thoroughly dreadful book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes the initial letters of some, truly, awful and book.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a go at something is making a try at it, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Visually challenged naval writer?

definitions.meaning: the blind beggar healed by Jesus in the Gospel of Mark
the pen name of Lewis Ricci, who wrote stories of the Royal Navy

explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel's sightless beggar of Jericho bears this name, which the Royal Navy officer Lewis Ricci also took as his pseudonym.

clue.text: Trollope's Plantaganet duke

parts.note: Plantagenet is here a first name: the politician who becomes Duke of Omnium in Trollope's political novels

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plantaganet' suggests the royal dynasty, but it is the first name of Trollope's statesman, Duke of Omnium, who gives the political novels their series name.
explanation.definitionFit: Plantagenet Palliser, later Duke of Omnium, is the central statesman of Trollope's political novels.

clue.text: Lambeth girl in first novel

parts.note: Somerset Maugham's first novel is named after a young working-class woman of Lambeth

explanation.walkthrough: Somerset Maugham's first novel, Liza of Lambeth (1897), is about a girl in that working-class district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Maugham's debut novel is titled after its heroine, a young factory girl from that London district.

clue.text: Legendary knight who visited Powell landmark novel

definitions.text: Legendary knight who visited Powell landmark novel

parts.words: Legendary knight who visited Powell landmark novel
parts.note: Anthony Powell's first novel is Afternoon Men; his Venusberg names the mountain of Venus that the German minstrel knight entered

explanation.walkthrough: Powell's early novel Venusberg is named after the mountain where Venus held court; the medieval minstrel-knight of legend, and of Wagner's opera, stayed there.
explanation.definitionFit: The German minstrel-knight of legend lingered in the Venusberg, the subject of Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Mechanical Shakespeare producer

parts.note: one of the rude mechanicals in A Midsummer Night's Dream, the carpenter who stages Pyramus and Thisbe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mechanical' looks like an adjective, but the rude mechanicals are the Athenian workmen in A Midsummer Night's Dream; Peter, the carpenter, directs their play.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter of this surname is the carpenter who organises the workmen's play in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Puzzle out crime involving brave young Veronese

indicators.note: to puzzle out is to work something out, and here the letters must be worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Solve a crime involving a courageous youth from Verona.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle' rearranges OUT CRIME. Romeo's witty friend in Romeo and Juliet is killed by Tybalt in Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo's bold friend in Shakespeare's tragedy is a young man of Verona.

clue.text: Incidentally heard in film

parts.note: a film's soundtrack is incidental, played in the background of the action

explanation.walkthrough: 'Incidentally' looks like 'by the way'; incidental music is the background score of a film or play.
explanation.definitionFit: A film's score is the incidental sound that accompanies the action, a composed accompaniment.

clue.text: Astringent Ulster graduates

parts.note: alum is a mineral salt used as an astringent
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called Ulster

explanation.surface: Sharp-tongued former students of a Northern Irish university.
explanation.walkthrough: Alum is used in styptic pencils to stop bleeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Former students of a college or school are its graduates, the Latin plural for old boys and girls.

clue.text: Rattigan's maid gets blame, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are put in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: A servant in a Rattigan play takes the fault for something gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges BLAME. Terence Rattigan was a British playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a domestic servant character in one of Terence Rattigan's plays.

clue.text: Take nothing from egg-shaped

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Take nothing from egg-shaped (4)': OVOID less O gives the letters, but no clue word defines the poet.

clue.text: Shoot Titus Groan, for example

definitions.meaning: a young plant shoot or twig cut for grafting
Titus is heir to the earldom of Gormenghast in Mervyn Peake's novels, an offspring of the noble line

explanation.definitionFit: A grafted twig is a cutting from a plant, and Peake's Titus is the heir and descendant of the Groans.

clue.text: Like Blake's volant annelid

parts.note: volant means flying and an annelid is a worm, recalling the worm 'that flies in the night' in The Sick Rose

explanation.walkthrough: Blake's poem The Sick Rose speaks of the unseen worm that flies in the night; volant means flying, and an annelid is a segmented worm.
explanation.definitionFit: Blake describes his flying worm as unseen, a creature beyond sight.

clue.text: Censured, like Connolly's playground

definitions.meaning: Cyril Connolly's essay collection The ... Playground (1945)

explanation.definitionFit: To denounce someone is to pass sentence on them, and Cyril Connolly titled his essay collection after a doomed playground.

clue.text: Laid by Ellis, in respect of attraction

definitions.text: Laid by Ellis, in respect of attraction

parts.words: Laid by Ellis, in respect of attraction
parts.note: Bret Easton Ellis wrote a novel about the principles of attraction, laid down as if regulations

explanation.walkthrough: Ellis looks like Havelock Ellis, the writer on sex, but it is Bret Easton Ellis, whose novel is The Rules of Attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulations are laid down, and Bret Easton Ellis's novel sets out those governing attraction.
